## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

MPC repeatedly solves a finite-horizon problem from an updated state estimate and applies an initial portion of the control. It may use nonlinear dynamics, constrained optimization and numerical methods that do not rely on superposition. Receding-horizon operation alone supplies neither feasibility nor stability guarantees.

iLQR uses first derivatives of the discrete dynamics in a local quadratic optimization; full DDP also retains second derivatives of that map. Both require a feedforward update as well as feedback, a forward nonlinear rollout and a step-acceptance procedure. Linear accumulation of first variations is one tool, not a definition of nonlinear control. See [the canonical derivation and limits](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-3-control.html).

## Overview

Modern nonlinear control algorithms exploit integral accumulation of
local linear structure.

## DDP and iLQR

Both methods rely on repeated linearization and integration.

## MPC

MPC applies integral superposition over a receding horizon.
